rounds.text: Yogi Infra Projects Ltd is deeply undervalued, trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.36x against a book value of ₹ 18.6 with the stock priced at ₹ 6.75 [E1], and a sector benchmark P/B of 1.29x [E6]. The company is actively deleveraging, successfully reducing its borrowings to Rs 45.88 Cr in Sep 2026 down from Rs 56.44 Cr a year earlier [E33]. Operational efficiency is also turning a corner, evidenced by a dramatic jump in operating margin to 10% in the trailing twelve months compared to just 1% three years prior [E24]. Furthermore, the business is generating robust cash, producing an operating cash flow of Rs 31.18 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 4.01 Cr in March 2026 [E29, E30], alongside a stellar 98% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E15]. Promoters share this confidence, increasing their stake to 44.60% by Sep 2026 from 43.90% in Dec 2023 [E35]. Conceded: the company carries a high debt-to-equity ratio of 1.47x [E31] and a low return on equity [E44].

Conceded: [E1]. The low price-to-book ratio of 0.36x [E1] masks fundamental distress when examined alongside long-term profitability metrics. The company generates a negligible return on equity, with median ROE figures over 10 years [E20], 5 years [E21], and 3 years [E22] remaining at or near 0%, alongside a TTM ROE of -0.39% [E8] and a flagged low 3-year ROE average of 0.63% [E44]. This chronic failure to generate returns explains why the stock has suffered a 1-year price decline of -35% [E19] and trades at a distressed P/E of -92.86x [E5]. Furthermore, working capital efficiency has deteriorated sharply, with debtor days ballooning from 49.9 to 105 days [E45] and working capital days surging from -38.0 days to an alarming 254 days [E46]. Leverage also presents a tangible risk, as debt-to-equity stands at 1.47x with borrowings exceeding net worth [E31], compounded by official warnings regarding a low interest coverage ratio [E43]. Finally, top-line deterioration is severe, evidenced by compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months plunging by -77% [E13].

Conceded: [E13]. However, the bear's focus on historical returns misses an active balance sheet de-leveraging and operational turnaround currently underway. While past ROE figures were low [E20, E21, E22], borrowings have actually decreased to Rs 45.88 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 56.44 Cr a year earlier [E33], directly countering the notion of unmitigated financial risk. The company generated substantial operating cash flow of Rs 31.18 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 4.01 Cr in Mar 2026 [E29, E30], proving cash generation capacity despite negative trailing profit metrics. Furthermore, promoters have increased their stake to 44.60% by Sep 2026 from 43.90% in Dec 2023 [E35], signaling strong insider conviction during this transition. Profit growth is also accelerating with a 98% expansion over the trailing twelve months [E15], and operating margins have improved by 9 percentage points over three years [E24]. Finally, the current valuation severely underappreciates these operational improvements, trading at a steep discount with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.36x [E1].

Conceded: [E33]. While borrowings decreased to Rs 45.88 Cr in Sep 2026 [E33], debt-to-equity sits at 1.47x because debt exceeds net worth, confirming active leverage risk [E31]. The cited operating and free cash flows of Rs 31.18 Cr and Rs 4.01 Cr for Mar 2026 [E29, E30] must be weighed against a cash conversion ratio of -148.48x and an explicit warning that it is a loss year where the ratio is not meaningful [E28]. The bull's reliance on a 98% trailing profit expansion [E15] ignores severe top-line contraction, specifically a compounded sales growth of -77% over the trailing twelve months [E13]. Furthermore, insider conviction via a 0.70 percentage point promoter stake increase [E35] does not erase structural operational headwinds, such as debtor days blowing out from 49.9 to 105 days [E45] and working capital days surging from -38.0 to 254 days [E46]. Finally, the 0.36x price-to-book valuation discount [E1] is fully justified by a persistent low interest coverage ratio [E43], a multi-year median ROE of 0% [E20, E21], and a negative ROE of -0.39% against a sector benchmark of 5.49% [E8].
